steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a small fluted tube pan.
Sift flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a bowl. Set aside.
Mix sugar, egg, and oil together in another bowl. Stir in the flour mixture just until combined; fold in apple, walnuts, and raisins. Pour into prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Fresh Apple Cake
raw_recipe.description: Grandma's wonderful fresh apple cake recipe is bursting with chunks of apples, raisins, walnuts, and spices for delicious flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Grandma's Fresh Apple Cake

review.reviewBody: It was so hot here today that I wanted a reminder of autumn! I doubled this so I could use my bundt pan and made the following adjustments to the recipe: added 2/3 cup dark brown sugar for a total of 1-2/3 c sugar instead of 2 cups; added 1 T vanilla; I shredded 2 large Braeburn apples and added 1/4 cup applesauce (for those that are tempted to add moisture to the thick batter, shred the apples and they will impart plenty of moisture--it will be like a normal cake batter once you get the apples mixed in) ; I didn't double the nuts--used 1/2 cup pecans; used 1 cup dates, no raisins; added a dash of nutmeg. Instead of doubling the oil, I was going to add 1/4 cup melted butter, but I forgot to add it--I didn't miss it at all. I would like to try it next time with 1/2 wheat flour. Now for the review: I love apple cake & my husband loves date cake--this is a perfect compromise. The cake is moist and flavorful and we both loved it. I added a glaze but it doesn't need anything to enhance it. It absolutely deserves 5 stars--thanks Steven!

Great flavor and baked well. I used Fuji apples. I changed the sugar to 3/4 cup and 1/4 cup brown sugar. Used 1 cup of melted butter in place of vegetable oil to give more flavor. Used 2 eggs to make it moist. Also added 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg to give more of a fall flavor. Came out perfect and was loved by everyone.

This recipe seems to be missing a moisture ingredient. As is I doubled the recipe...it was very dry and crumbly so I added about 11.5 ounces of applesauce to the doubled amount which made it more like a cake batter! It turned out moist and delicious! I had enough for one bundt cake and six small muffins.

I added a bit of plain greek yogurt (also 2 pinches of cornstarch), tad bit more evoo, cinnamon & allspice & 1 Tbsp toasted wheat germ. Almost forgot, I used dark brown sugar instead of white for a more robust flavor And definitely cooked it for 45 minutes at 335°. It was moist n delicious!

This turned out exactly what I was hoping for! Moist with lots of fruits and nuts, and just enough batter to hold it all together. While making the batter I was concerned that it wasn't enough to incorporate all of the fruit and nuts, and it did take a strong arm to mix it all together! The results, however, were marvelous! I made some minor adjustments; reducing sugar to 3/4 cup and I did use dates and not raisins. I did not have the correct size loaf pan (mine is 9x5) and it did take a little longer to bake than the suggested time. It tastes terrific, however, even if I did cut into it too soon! Some ice cream on top of the warm slice would have been just about perfect! This recipe is a keeper!

As written it fits a 5x9 (cooked for 45 min) but would also fit in a 4x8 since it didn’t fill the pan. Chopped the apple in fairly small bits. Thought I had raisins but they were dried cherries. Soaked them in some peach schnapps for a few minutes but would use raisins next time. I always soak raisins but it probably doesn’t matter. Added vanilla and teaspoon nutmeg again not needed but I love nutmeg. I thought the batter was fine not crumbly at all. Amazing flavor!!! Will make this again and again. What I especially like is the size. Doesn’t take long to chop up a few apples and make it. A keeper recipe for sore.

This was so freaking good. I shredded one apple and diced the other. I used half brown and half white sugar. 1/8 c. oil and 1/4 c. apple sauce.
I also used golden raisins and pecans.
I will cut the sugar to 3/4 c. and use melted butter instead of oil. Honestly, this is great as it is. Kudos.
I've been a member here for many years and I think this may be my 3rd review. 
Also so easy to make vegan and healtheri,

It is fantastic. Few things ... I used 1/2 raisins and 1/2 dates vs one or other. I used cooking Splenda vs sugar. And I used 1/2 white flour and 1/2 whole wheat flour vs all white. I found the batter mixture a tad thick before adding the apples so I added 1/4 cup of plain Greek yogurt to the mix. Cooked for 55 min. Super tasty and moist.

love the recipe, but cut the sugar in half, added a teaspoon of vanilla, added an extra 1/2 teaspoon of Cinnamon. saved 1 tablespoon of the flour and mixed in with the nuts and raisins before added to the batter to help prevent from ending up on the bottom of the cake.

Delicious! Recipe as stated is for loaf cake size (not bundt, which needs a double recipe). I did reduce sugar to 2/3 C, using half light brown and half white, and it was plenty sweet. For 9x5 pan, bake time was about 40 min.

Delish and moist. Not dense or claggy. Doubled it for a bundt pan and added 1 shredded apple to the recipe to allow for a bit less oil. plumped up the raisins w/a bit of bourbon and used toasted pecans. Husband loved it. Will make again.

The amounts of baking soda and salt are disproportionately high for the amount of flour. The cake looks great but is completely inedible because all one can taste is salt. All the ingredients are typical for this kind of pastry, but I would use baking powder rather than baking soda. I had learned before that soda can be tricky, in that too much of it renders the bake too salty. I regret ignoring my experience and following the recipe to the letter.
Very dense. Really needs to be redone. Not very happy. Would have been better as a muffin.

Delicious! Used craisins and walnuts and added some cinnamon and sugar to the apples after chopping them. Also added nutmeg and ginger to the cinnamon in the batter and cut back sugar to 1 cup as we don't like cakes too sweet.

I used butter instead of oil. I added 1 1/2 tsps of cinnamon. I added 2 tsp of vanilla to the butter mixture. It looks like the apple batter mixture is off but it is perfect after it baked. It is a great dessert with coffee. You could even eat it for breakfast.

I thought this cake turned out lovely! I used a 10 cup Bundt pan that was a bit on the narrower side, and it filled it about 2/3rds full. So it doesn't make a large cake, but that's ok. Also, my cake only needed 50 minutes to bake, so I would start checking for doneness at around the 40 minute mark, depending on the size of your pan. Otherwise, the flavor is great! It's got the right amount of sweetness and spice; and the apples come through brilliantly. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

There definitely is a missing liquid ingredient in this recipe. Using only the called for 1/4 cup of oil produced a dry, crumbly mix that couldn’t even incorporate all the flour. I added more oil and some milk, which definitely helped. Please proofread your recipes before posting them.
This was perfect for two people. I made mini 5 mini bundt cakes. I added a little clove and extra cinnamon. I dusted them with powdered sugar and they made a lovely fall dessert.
Instead of oil, I used applesauce
I added 1/2 tsp vanilla, 1/2 cup applesauce. Also I used 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white. I used two big apples so more than 2 cups. It looks perfect—hope it tastes that good.
